source.title: Mini-batch size sensitivity in deep residual networks for short-term load forecasting: an empirical study
source.authors: Jun-Chen Liu; Faisul Arif Ahmad; K. Samsudin; F. Hashim; M. A. Ab. Kadir

record.file_problem: Complete article text supplied; manuscript identifies itself as an unedited Article in Press.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size effects on held-out forecasting performance in residual networks for electricity load time series, extending batch-size findings to a new task setting.
record.gate_note: The study varies mini-batch size and reports held-out forecasting metrics. It does not use random labels or report training error, so it cannot test whether networks that memorize arbitrary labels generalize to natural labels, or directly measure a train-test error gap. Cited batch-size results from other studies are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study varies batch size with a fixed 700-epoch budget and otherwise fixed training settings, measuring held-out forecasting error. This tests V5's batch-size effect in a new setting: electricity-load regression with Adam and snapshot ensembling.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' batch-size conclusion: 64 gives the lowest MAPE in all three model–dataset settings, 32 is competitive, and prediction-point bootstrap comparisons favor 64 significantly. Their claims about gradient noise, sharp minima, and optimization stability are interpretations rather than directly measured mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Adam, fixed 700-epoch training and snapshot ensembling on real-world load-forecasting time series; it varies batch size but does not reproduce the cited image-classification or language-model experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out MAPE varies with batch size and dataset/model setting; batch size 64 is best among those tested. The authors state that interactions with learning-rate schedules, optimizer variants, and adaptive training strategies were not systematically explored.
record.peer_reviewed: Scientific Reports; Article in Press in the supplied text
record.problems: The evaluation covers two real-world electricity systems and does not directly report training error or a train-test gap. The study holds the optimizer and other training settings fixed, so it does not establish whether the batch-size pattern changes under other recipes.
record.rows_left_out: None of the extracted batch-size MAPE results or bootstrap comparisons were left out. Other reported metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE, NMSE, R, and R²) are omitted because the study reports them alongside MAPE for the same conditions and they do not disagree with it.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width scaling beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer performance under different tuning budgets.
Image classification and language modeling; whether longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes remove the penalty.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: V5 already allows a workload-dependent threshold, so improvement from batches 8 through 64 does not warrant a scope-limiting or challenging verdict. The forecasting setting is an extension of V5, not evidence against its named benchmarks. No training-error measurements are needed to compare held-out performance, but a train–test gap cannot be inferred. Bootstrap uncertainty reflects resampled prediction errors, not variation across independent training runs; significance is reported only for 32 versus 64, not for the larger-batch penalties. Batch size was selected using the reported test results, with no separate validation selection described.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.

Image-classification and language benchmarks; workload-dependent batch thresholds; alternate training recipes such as longer training, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes; the study does not report training error or directly measure the train-test gap.
Dropout interventions and their effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: DRN on ISO-NE, batches 128–512 versus 64, fixed 700 epochs
relationships.reason: R5–R7 report MAPE rising from the R4 baseline of 0.016695 to 0.020716, 0.021941, and 0.025728.
relationships.display_finding: The study's results suggest that forecasting mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) increased as batch size grew on ISO-NE. These results have not been verified.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: DRN and PCA-DRN on ISO-NE and MyPJ across all tested batch sizes
reader_labels.reason: The best held-out forecasting results occur at medium batch size 64; the smallest batches also perform worse, and the data are time-series forecasting rather than the image or language tasks named in V5 (R1–R21).
